about: Betsson is a Swedish online gambling group operating casino, sports betting, poker and bingo brands including Betsson, Betsafe, NordicBet, Casinoeuro and Betsson Sport, in Europe, Latin America and Africa. Customers are consumers across dozens of licensed markets, and revenue is gaming income of around 1 billion euros. Listed on Nasdaq Stockholm (BETS B). Strong awareness in Nordic and Latin American markets, and a history of major sports sponsorship including football. Gambling sponsorship is restricted in many F1 markets.

Online gambling and gaming group behind PokerStars, Full Tilt, BetStars and Sky Bet (via Sky Betting and Gaming, acquired in 2018), founded in 2001 as Amaya's PokerStars business and based in Douglas, Isle of Man. Listed in Toronto and on Nasdaq (TSG), it merged with Flutter Entertainment in 2020. Customers are online poker players and sports bettors in regulated markets. Strong consumer brand, with a sponsorship history including Ferrari and Premier League partnerships.

Philippine company that provides online gaming and e-games technology and services, historically working with the government gaming regulator PAGCOR on electronic bingo, e-games stations and internet gambling systems. Customers include state gaming bodies and licensed operators, and revenue came from system and service fees. It is listed on the Philippine Stock Exchange and has seen its business shrink with regulatory changes in the sector. Mostly B2B with modest consumer visibility. Gambling-related, which would limit its fit as a sponsor in many markets.

Online gaming operator offering sports betting and casino in Spain, Mexico, Argentina, Colombia and Panama, a spin-off of Codere Group, Spain's long-established gaming company. Revenue about EUR 250m. Listed on Nasdaq (CDRO). Consumer brand in Latin America and Spain, with a long record of sports sponsorship. Codere Online markets through websites and apps with a focus on betting in Spain, Mexico and Argentina, and was listed via a SPAC merger in 2021.

Kindred Group is a Malta-based online gambling group, operating the Unibet, 32Red, Maria Casino, Bingo.com and Storspelare brands, covering sports betting, casino, poker and bingo for consumers in Europe, Australia and the US. It makes money from betting and gaming margins and employs about 2,000 people. Unibet is a prominent sports-betting name with sponsorship deals in football and other sports. It was listed on Nasdaq Stockholm, and in 2024 it was acquired by France's Francaise des Jeux (FDJ UNITED). Gambling advertising is restricted in many markets, but the brand has strong sport sponsorship experience.

Canadian operator of casinos and entertainment venues, with more than 25 properties in British Columbia, Ontario, Alberta and Nova Scotia, covering slots, table games, restaurants and live entertainment. Revenue comes from gambling plus food and beverage. Privately held by financial investors, with a refinancing in 2020. Moderately known as a consumer brand in Western Canada, but gaming sponsorship carries advertising rules and reputational sensitivities.

US regional casino operator listed on Nasdaq (FLL), headquartered in Las Vegas. Owns casinos including Silver Slipper in Mississippi, Rising Star in Indiana, Bronco Billy's and the new Chamonix resort in Colorado, and others in Nevada. Customers are local gamblers and tourists in regional markets, revenue from gaming, hotel and food and beverage. Small to mid-sized operator with modest brand awareness beyond its local markets.

Swiss sports data and technology firm based in St Gallen supplying live data, odds, and integrity monitoring to sportsbooks and leagues, with rights deals with the NBA, NFL, UEFA and others. Customers include betting operators, media and sports bodies in dozens of countries, with revenue from data feeds, odds services and trading tools plus its Sportradar Integrity Services and Sportradar Ad:s offerings. Nasdaq listed as SRAD since 2021. B2B with strong sports industry presence.

LIV Golf is a professional golf league launched in 2022 that is funded by Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund, with 54-hole team events, big prize money and players such as Jon Rahm and Bryson DeChambeau. Run from the UK and US by Greg Norman as chief and later by Scott O'Neil. Funding shown is about 6.5 billion dollars. Prominent in sports media and a controversy for sportswashing concerns. High sports visibility and an active sponsorship portfolio.

Marriott International is the world's largest hotel company by rooms, with over 9,000 properties and 30 brands such as Ritz-Carlton, St. Regis, W, Sheraton, Westin, Courtyard, JW Marriott and Marriott Bonvoy loyalty with over 200 million members. Earns franchise and management fees, with revenue near 25 billion dollars. Headquartered in Bethesda, Maryland; founded 1927. Listed on Nasdaq (MAR). Very strong consumer brands with significant sports and events partnerships.

Invited Clubs (formerly ClubCorp) is an Irving, Texas operator of private golf, country, athletic and city clubs, with about 200 clubs in the US, plus Invited Hospitality events. It earns membership dues, initiation fees and food and beverage revenue from members. Owned by Apollo Global Management, which bought ClubCorp in 2017 and rebranded it in 2021. Private. Upscale brand, recognised by golfers and affluent members, with some golf-related sponsorship activity.

PureGym is a Leeds-based low-cost gym operator, one of the largest in Europe, with around 600 sites and about 2 million members in the UK, Switzerland, Denmark, Saudi Arabia and Mexico. It earns monthly membership fees, with no contracts, and has expanded via acquisitions including Fitness Park in France. Owned by Leonard Green & Partners after buying it from KKR-backed owners in 2021. Private. Strong UK consumer brand with substantial advertising, including football partnerships.

San Diego Padres is the Major League Baseball franchise of San Diego, California, playing at Petco Park in the National League West. It earns from ticket sales, sponsorship, media rights and merchandising. Controlled by the Seidler family and partners after the death of Peter Seidler in 2023. Private. A large local fan base and a sports property that itself sells sponsorship inventory, rather than a corporate buyer.

Hello TransTech, formerly HelloBike, is a Shanghai-based Chinese mobility company running the Hello app, which offers shared bikes, shared e-bikes and mopeds, ride-hailing and related services, plus battery swap and EV services. Backed by Ant Group and other investors, with about $2 billion raised. Serves tens of millions of consumers in China. Widely known consumer app brand in China.

Very high consumer awareness in Canada and a sponsor of sports and charity events.

It serves over 60 million customers in about 190 countries, with revenue of about 17 billion pounds and operations in the UK, Australia, Spain, Chile, Hong Kong and more. Strong consumer brand in the UK, Australia and elsewhere, with sports and arts sponsorships.

Station Casinos is a Las Vegas, Nevada casino and gaming operator, part of Red Rock Resorts (Nasdaq: RRR), owning Red Rock, Green Valley Ranch, Palace Station, Boulder Station and other locals-focused casino resorts. It earns revenue from gaming, hotel, dining and entertainment, mostly from Las Vegas residents. Controlled by the Fertitta family. Strong local brand in Las Vegas, with limited recognition elsewhere.

Equinox Group is a US luxury fitness company headquartered in New York, operating high-end Equinox clubs, SoulCycle studios, Blink Fitness and the Equinox Hotels brand, with about 100 clubs and premium memberships costing hundreds of dollars a month. It also sells digital fitness and Equinox+ products. Founded 1991, owned by private investors led by Related Companies' Stephen Ross and Vornado. Revenue is about 1 billion dollars. Premium lifestyle consumer brand appealing to affluent urban customers.

Peloton Interactive is a US connected fitness company headquartered in New York and listed on Nasdaq (PTON). It sells Peloton bikes, treads and rowers and a subscription to live and on-demand classes, with around 2.9 million subscribers and revenue near 2.5 billion dollars. Founded 2012; its COVID boom was followed by layoffs and a restructuring under CEO Peter Stern. Customers are home fitness enthusiasts. Strong consumer brand with extensive partnerships and advertising.

Basic-Fit is Europe's largest budget fitness chain, operating about 1,500 gyms in the Netherlands, Belgium, France, Spain, Luxembourg and Germany, with several million members paying low monthly fees and using an app for classes and training. Headquartered in Hoofddorp, founded in 2007, with revenue of about 1.2 billion euros or more. Listed on Euronext Amsterdam (BFIT). Strong consumer brand in its home markets with heavy advertising.

Cult.fit, formerly Curefit, is an Indian health and fitness company running Cult gyms and group fitness centres, Cult at-home and digital classes, mind.fit, plus nutrition, health care and a sports gear line, Curefit Healthcare, with centres in about 20 cities. Founded in 2016 and based in Bangalore by Mukesh Bansal and Ankit Nagori, with Tata Digital as a major investor. Has raised about $684 million. Private. Strong consumer fitness brand in India with celebrity and sports marketing.

The Chicago Bulls are the NBA basketball franchise based in Chicago, owned by Jerry Reinsdorf's group since 1985, playing at the United Center and winning six NBA championships in the Michael Jordan era. Revenue comes from tickets, media rights, merchandise and sponsorship, with a franchise valued at over $4 billion. Crunchbase shows about $645 million in funding. A sports property rather than a typical corporate sponsor, but a global consumer brand.

U.S. Physical Therapy is the operator of one of the largest US networks of outpatient physical and occupational therapy clinics, with about 700 or more clinics, plus an industrial injury prevention business. Revenue comes from patient visits billed to insurers and Medicare, at around $700 million annually. Headquartered in Houston, Texas, founded in 1990. Listed on NYSE (USPH). Healthcare services brand, local rather than national consumer recognition.

Hybar is a steel producer that builds and operates a scrap metal recycling steel mill in Osceola, Arkansas, producing rebar and other long steel products from recycled metal. Customers are construction and infrastructure contractors. Crunchbase shows about $1.8 billion in funding, large for a single mill and probably reflecting a major project investment. Private. B2B industrial brand with little consumer awareness.

about: Brunswick Corporation is a US maker of recreational marine products and fitness equipment. Brands include Mercury Marine outboard engines, Sea Ray, Bayliner, Boston Whaler and Lund boats, Navico Group marine electronics (Simrad, Lowrance), and the Life Fitness and Cybex gyms equipment businesses. Customers are boat owners, dealers, boat builders and commercial gyms; annual revenue is about 5 to 6 billion dollars. Founded in 1845, headquartered in Mettawa, Illinois (earlier Lake Forest), listed on the NYSE (BC). Strong recreational brands and an existing marine racing presence.

Diamond Sports Group was the owner of the Bally Sports regional sports networks, which carried local broadcast rights for dozens of MLB, NBA and NHL teams. It was created in 2019 when Sinclair Broadcast Group bought 21 regional networks from Disney and Fox for 10.6 billion dollars. Based in Norfolk, Virginia, it filed for Chapter 11 in 2023 after cord-cutting and rights fee pressures and emerged in 2024 as Main Street Sports Group, rebranded FanDuel Sports Network. Revenue came from cable and satellite carriage fees and advertising. Formerly well known to sports fans in the United States.

Real Madrid C.F. is the Spanish football club, member-owned and based in Madrid, 15-time European Cup and Champions League winner and one of the most valuable sports franchises globally, with annual revenue above 1 billion euros. It earns income from matchday, broadcasting, commercial sponsorships and merchandising at the Santiago Bernabeu stadium, plus basketball and other sports. Its global following runs into hundreds of millions; sponsors include Emirates, Adidas and Hewlett Packard Enterprise. Very high consumer visibility; already an elite sponsor-seeking property that may compete with F1 for budgets.

Inspired Entertainment is a global gaming technology company supplying server-based gaming machines, virtual sports, digital games and interactive content to casinos, betting shops, lotteries and online operators. Customers are regulated gambling operators in the UK, Italy, North America and other markets, and it earns revenue from leased terminals and game licensing. Its virtual sports were once used by UK bookmakers such as William Hill and Ladbrokes. Headquartered in New York with large UK operations, listed on Nasdaq (INSE), with revenue around 300 million dollars. B2B gambling supplier with limited consumer brand awareness; regulated sector.

The New England Patriots are the National Football League franchise in Foxborough, Massachusetts, owned by the Kraft family since 1994, and winners of six Super Bowls during the Tom Brady and Bill Belichick era. The team plays at Gillette Stadium and revenue comes from NFL broadcasting rights, sponsorship, ticketing and merchandise. The franchise is valued at roughly 7 billion dollars or more. The Kraft Group also owns MLS club New England Revolution. Very high US consumer visibility and an existing global fan base, notably in the UK and Germany through NFL international games.

SEGG Media Corporation is a US-listed holding company, based in Spicewood, Texas, formerly Lottery.com, a lottery ticket management and online lottery platform. It has been repositioned toward sports, media and gaming, including a Spanish sports media and marketing business associated with sports stars, and its share listing is on Nasdaq (SEGG). It has had a turbulent history, including an SEC investigation, and a very small revenue base. Funding shown is about 774 million dollars, which looks inflated by non-standard financing. Limited brand awareness; treat with caution on credibility.

Huge global fan base and an elite sports sponsorship property.

Umicore is a Belgian materials technology and recycling group, making battery materials for electric vehicles, catalysts for car emissions, and recycled precious metals, with revenue of several billion euros and roughly 11,000 employees. Acushnet Holdings is a US golf equipment company, based in Fairhaven, Massachusetts, owner of Titleist golf balls and clubs and FootJoy shoes and gloves, plus Scotty Cameron, Vokey and KJUS. Solmate Infrastructure is a Dublin-based company that, via its rebranding of Brera Holdings in 2025, became a Solana-focused digital asset treasury and node infrastructure business, listed on Nasdaq (SLMT). Circuit of The Americas (COTA) is a motorsports and entertainment venue in Austin, Texas, which opened in 2012 and hosts the Formula 1 United States Grand Prix, MotoGP's Americas Grand Prix, IMSA and other events, plus concerts and festivals. It is a 3.4-mile track owned by Bobby Epstein and partners. Customers are fans, teams and corporate guests. High-profile F1 venue, an existing F1 partner.

The Miami Marlins are a Major League Baseball team based in Miami, Florida, playing at loanDepot park, with World Series titles in 1997 and 2003. A professional sports franchise, with a regional fan base and an existing sponsorship business.

Major League Volleyball is a US women's professional volleyball league, with teams in Texas and other US cities, formed from the merger of the Pro Volleyball Federation and Athletes Unlimited Pro Volleyball.
